description:
rfc8398.rs:338 declares `fn mailbox_equivalent(rfc822: &str, smtputf8: &str) -> Result<bool, &'static str>` with three distinct error conditions ('no @ delimiter', 'empty local-part or domain', 'U-label → A-label conversion failed') encoded as string literals. The review-rusty error-handling rules explicitly flag this: 'error variants that wrap String for the message instead of structured fields'.

The helper is module-private, so the cost of restructuring is small. Options:

1. Define a private `MailboxParseError` enum with three variants (MissingAt, EmptyPart { which: Field }, IdnaFailed). Internally typed errors cost ~10 LoC of impl Display.
2. If callers (in practice, just `check_cert`) only care 'malformed in any way', return `Option<bool>` and lose the distinction. Combined with the .unwrap_or_default() finding (PKIX-hy2e.35), this is the simpler restructuring.

The principled fix depends on how the call site is restructured under PKIX-hy2e.35. If the call site moves to up-front validation, the helper becomes infallible (`fn mailbox_equivalent -> bool`) and the error type goes away entirely. That's the cleanest outcome and likely the right answer; this finding then closes as a duplicate of .35.
title: mailbox_equivalent uses stringly-typed &'static str error in internal helper
